pairs.subject: time-travel-replay
pairs.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/timestrip/TimeStrip.tsx:3 This context's only time-based shapes are TimeStrip, a settled per-day histogram whose drag sets a {from,to} filter range (the 'settled-record view' the golden path puts outside replay), and Wave, an audio take's peak strip (media-playback). A search of the seven component dirs for the subject's terms found no hit for scrub/seek/rewind. 'replay' appears only in a comment saying the prototype's replayed session segment was dropped, and 'playhead' only as the audio playhead, so no completed run is re-presented under a viewer-owned clock.

techniques.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/timestrip/TimeStrip.tsx:3 The day buckets are a static map of the whole record, not a playable timeline with a moving now.
packages/ui/src/components/timestrip/TimeStrip.tsx:11 The drag is a range brush for filtering. There is no play/pause/seek/speed transport and no replay clock.
packages/ui/src/components/timestrip/strip.ts:14 The one replayed feed the prototype had was removed, so there is no replay feed to share or fork a renderer for.
packages/ui/src/components/wave/Wave.tsx:13 This playhead is an audio take's position (media-playback), not a fold over run records, so keyframes and prefix sums do not come into it.
packages/ui/src/components/header/header.ts:8 Spend is a settled sum over a time window that is never re-accrued against a replay position.

packages/ui/src/components/eventrow/EventRow.tsx:68 Derived times are marked on each datum in a static list, which is sound on its own terms, but nothing is played back, so the rule for keeping the label visible during playback has nothing to govern.
